title: Majority Fourier weight limit
statement: For every odd natural number $k$, let $L_k=\frac{4}{\pi k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$. The level-$k$ Fourier weight of majority on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+1$ converges to $L_k$ as $m$ tends to infinity. Moreover, for every natural number $m$ with $k\le (2m+1)/2$, where the quotient is rounded down, its level-$k$ Fourier weight lies between $L_k$ and $\left(1+\frac{2k}{2m+1}\right)L_k$.
hypotheses_covered: For the bounds, $m$ is a natural number
For the bounds, $k\le (2m+1)/2$ using natural-number division
replaced:
For each $q\in\mathbb N$, define $M_q:\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when
more than $q$ coordinates equal $1$, and $-1$ otherwise; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2q+1\}$ define
$\widehat M_q(S)=2^{-(2q+1)}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}}M_q(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_q)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_q(S)^2$.
For each fixed odd integer $k\ge1$, set
$L_k=\frac{4}{\pi k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$; then
$\lim_{m\to\infty}W_k(M_m)=L_k$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$ satisfying
$k\le\lfloor(2m+1)/2\rfloor$ one has
\[
 L_k\le W_k(M_m)\le\left(1+\frac{2k}{2m+1}\right)L_k.
\]
